title: Weak point Wednesday: Trapezius
summary: NH covers trap growth for naturals. Insertions matter (his small clavicles make his traps look big), and naturals can build impressive traps even though traps respond strongly to androgens. Deadlifts alone stop working once the deadlift stalls, so he adds heavy snatch-grip shrugs emphasising the stretch, partials, and a brutal rule (borrowed from AlphaDestiny): end every pull set with shrugs, then a weighted stretch hold.

claims.claim: Trap size depends a lot on insertions.
Traps have many androgen receptors and blow up with hormones, which is why disproportionately big traps are seen as a fake-natty tell; still, naturals can build impressive traps.
While making a 10-year transformation video he found he had good traps even before lifting, likely because his small clavicles make the trap insertion area small so they look bigger.
With a small frame you should develop peripheral muscles (traps, delts, triceps, forearms) as much as possible to look wider.
'Just get a bigger deadlift' for traps works only until the deadlift stalls, limited by the posterior chain; traps are stronger since they can hold far more weight over a shorter range.
Some people can rack pull above the knee with 1000 lb but barely deadlift 500 lb, because the shorter range is much easier.

numbers.load: 1000 lb rack pull vs 500 lb deadlift

claims.claim: His deadlift-only approach stalled his deadlift and trap growth for years; he then added partials and shrugs, borrowing much of his approach from AlphaDestiny.
Compounds like deadlifts, snatch-grip deadlifts, overhead press and pin press add trap volume without being trap isolation.
For heavy trap isolation he does snatch-grip shrugs up to 400 lb, focusing on letting the weight stretch the traps; full ROM isn't necessary because the stretch is what matters.
He also uses trap-focused Yates row variations for heavy trap work.
Rule for trap volume: end every set of any pull from the floor (from 135 up to 405) with shrugs; when you can no longer shrug, hold and let the weight stretch the traps until you must let go.
He has done this shrug-finisher rule for three weeks, pulling from the floor every two days; it's painful and exhausting and made his traps insanely sore, but he's already seeing size gains.
Weighted stretching is an underexplored, highly effective method for many (not all) muscle groups: a muscle stretched under load grows.
Traps are among the most resilient muscles; he has never heard of anyone tearing a trap, which is why aggressive weighted stretching works for them.
For lagging traps, floor pulls and clean shrugs aren't enough: add high pulls, rack pulls, heavy cheated shrugs with a stretch, and the shrug-finisher superset.
